title: Bats
subtitle: Seeing with sound
summary: In 1793 Lazzaro Spallanzani blinded bats and found they still flew round a room strung with threads. Nobody could say how until 1938, when a Harvard undergraduate, Donald Griffin, held bats up to a physicist's ultrasonic detector and heard them calling. The course follows the calls from there, including why a bat closing on a moth speeds up to 200 calls a second and how tiger moths click back to jam them, before turning to how two grams of fat last a little brown bat the winter and why vampire bats feed hungry roost-mates. Three branches take you to a breadboard detector you can build, the fifteen species of Washington State at dusk over Green Lake, and the 1943 bat bomb.
